type.$description: Typography scale for johnthedesigner.com. Three-font system: Schmaltzy (self-hosted VF, display only), Fraunces (Google Fonts, headings), Nunito Sans (Google Fonts, body/UI). Named semantic roles — content-sparse, editorial-leaning. Scale is hand-tuned from a loose 1.25–1.33 modular base to land on clean values with correct line-height grid relationships. All line-heights are unitless multipliers. Legibility constraints applied per role.

display.$description: Hero headline — Schmaltzy heavy blackletter. One instance per page maximum. Used only for the primary page title (home hero, case study title, about header). The personality anchor of the system.

font-family.$description: Self-hosted variable font. next/font/local from /fonts/Schmaltzy-VF.ttf. Falls back to serif.

font-size.$description: At content-sparse density, display lives at 64px. Adjust to 56px on viewports below 768px.

font-weight.$description: Heavy weight. Schmaltzy is a variable font — 800 is the target; adjust if the VF axis range differs.

line-height.$description: Tight. At 64px, 1.0 line-height is correct — display text is rarely multi-line; tight setting is intentional.

letter-spacing.$description: Slight negative tracking compensates for optical spread at 64px. Standard for display sizes.

heading-lg.$description: Major section heading — Fraunces SemiBold. Case study section titles, work index page heading, about page H1. The primary structural heading role.

font-family.$description: Google Font — next/font/google. Georgia as system fallback.

font-size.$description: 34px — clean step below display. 64 → 34 is a clear hierarchy jump that reads at a glance.

font-weight.$description: SemiBold. Creates hierarchy against heading-sm (weight 400) without approaching display weight.

line-height.$description: 1.15 — correct for 28–40px range per architecture reference. Tight but allows multi-line headings to breathe.

letter-spacing.$description: Negative tracking at 34px. Standard optical correction for large headings.

heading-sm.$description: Subsection heading — Fraunces Regular. Case study subsection headers, card headings, about section subheads. Lower visual tension than heading-lg — feels editorial rather than structural.

font-size.$description: 22px — clean step below heading-lg. Falls in the 18–24px range where line-height 1.25–1.35 is correct.

font-weight.$description: Regular. Deliberately lower weight than heading-lg — role distinction communicated through weight difference, not size alone.

line-height.$description: 1.25 — tighter than body, looser than heading-lg. Correct for 18–24px range.

deck.$description: Case study deck / subhead — Fraunces Light Italic. Appears directly beneath the display title as editorial bridge copy before body text begins. Also usable as a pull quote or chapter intro. Italic provides warmth and pace contrast.

font-size.$description: 20px — slightly larger than body-lg, clearly subordinate to headings. Clean value in the 18–24px comfort zone.

font-weight.$description: Light. The weight drop from heading-sm (400) is intentional — deck copy recedes.

line-height.$description: 1.4 — generous for a size that may be used in multi-line deck copy. Sits between heading and body line-height values.

letter-spacing.$description: Zero tracking. Fraunces Light Italic has calibrated defaults at this size; no adjustment needed.

font-style.$description: Always italic for this role. The italic is part of the role definition, not an optional state.

body-lg.$description: Primary body prose — Nunito Sans Regular. About page copy, case study body paragraphs, long-form content. The reading workhorse of the system. Sized and spaced for sustained reading.

font-family.$description: Google Font — next/font/google. Falls back to system-ui.

font-size.$description: 17px — slightly above the conventional 16px. Reflects content-sparse density; there is room for slightly larger body text. Nunito Sans has a moderate x-height — 17px reads clearly without feeling large.

font-weight.$description: Regular. Body text should never be set bold; weight carries semantic meaning at this role.

line-height.$description: 1.7 — generous for a reading context. 17px × 1.7 = 28.9px line height, close to a 4px grid multiple of 28px. Aids comprehension for extended reading. Architecture reference: body range is 1.4–1.6; 1.7 is deliberately above this for content-sparse editorial context.

letter-spacing.$description: Zero tracking. Nunito Sans body at 17px uses font defaults. No adjustment needed.

body-sm.$description: Secondary body prose — Nunito Sans Regular. Card body copy, work index descriptions, sidebar content, secondary descriptions. One size step below body-lg; same weight and family for consistency.

font-size.$description: 14px — clear step below 17px. Sits at the lower boundary of comfortable reading; do not use at smaller sizes for prose.

font-weight.$description: Regular. Matches body-lg weight — consistency in prose, differentiation only by size.

line-height.$description: 1.65 — slightly tighter than body-lg (1.7) for a smaller size, still generous. 14px × 1.65 = 23.1px, near 24px grid.

letter-spacing.$description: Zero tracking at 14px. Slight positive tracking could be added if a specific typeface requires it.

label.$description: UI chrome label — Nunito Sans Bold, uppercase, tracked. Eyebrow labels, section category tags, nav metadata, timestamps, form field labels. The uppercase + tracking combination creates strong visual signal at 11px. Always uppercase — never set label-scale text in sentence or title case.

font-size.$description: 11px — UI-chrome scale. Below this, legibility degrades; at this size, bold + tracking is required.

font-weight.$description: Bold. Weight 700 is essential at 11px — lighter weights at this size become illegible, especially in uppercase.

line-height.$description: 1.0 — label text is typically single-line UI chrome. No line-height expansion needed.

letter-spacing.$description: Positive tracking is required at uppercase 11px. 0.12em opens the letter spacing to compensate for optical compression of uppercase characters at small sizes. Architecture reference: small sizes require slight positive tracking.

caption.$description: Supporting text — Nunito Sans Regular. Image captions, footnotes, input helper text, timestamps in secondary contexts. Always on-surface-muted (slate-500) — never on-surface (slate-900).

font-size.$description: 12px — clearly smaller than body-sm, clearly larger than true fine print. Comfortable for supplementary content.

font-weight.$description: Regular. Caption text should recede; weight would draw unwanted attention.

line-height.$description: 1.5 — appropriate for 12px. Architecture reference: small/label range is 1.3–1.5.

letter-spacing.$description: Tiny positive tracking at 12px aids legibility at this size without visible effect.

code.$description: Monospace code — Geist Mono. Inline code snippets, code blocks in case studies, technical labels in Sistema/Paletteer contexts. Loads as part of the Geist type system alongside display roles.

font-family.$description: Geist Mono via next/font/google. Falls back to system monospace stack.

font-size.$description: 13px — monospace fonts appear larger than proportional fonts at the same size due to wide characters. 13px in Geist Mono visually matches 14px in Nunito Sans.

font-weight.$description: Regular. Bold mono weight is reserved for syntax highlighting (specific token categories), not the base style.

line-height.$description: 1.6 — slightly tighter than body-lg. Code blocks benefit from a bit less leading than prose; lines are shorter and scanning is more vertical.

letter-spacing.$description: Zero tracking. Monospace fonts have fixed character widths; tracking adjustments distort the alignment properties.
